# error handling

When to read: an action returns `{"error": ...}`. Read this file and follow the rules. Do not read for normal calls.

## Error-code actions

On `{"error": ...}`, extract `code=<error-code>` and act by the rules below. Safe `msg` is used only to add parameter / state / restricted-object context. Scripts and outer wrappers must not invent next steps; when multiple layers wrap a code, the innermost backend business code wins and only one rule fires. Error codes are for model decisions; convert to natural language when shown to the user, never expose the internal code.

1. **`11607` / `INVALID_PARAMS`, msg contains 「不支持语音解析」 — format not supported**: tell the user this format has no transcript parsing, stating the current format and the server's supported-format list; if needed, suggest re-uploading in a supported audio format. No retry.
2. **`11007`, `11607`, `56040`, `400` / `HTTP_400`, `413` / `HTTP_413`, `422` / `HTTP_422`, `INVALID_PARAMS`; or no code but local param-validation failure — invalid params**: correct the failing param, taking the correct format from the current module `entry.md` / script `--help`; ask the user if uncertain. Retry max 1. Exception (library doc direct edit): `11607` on an `update` action is not a param error — target inside a `TableCell`: switch to whole-table replacement per `doc/tasks/table_edit.md` §2; any other text block: direct-edit `update` is dead end-to-end, switch to `insert_after` + `delete` pair per `doc/content_contract.md` §4. No verbatim retry.
3. **`E_NOT_WORKBUDDY` — not in the WorkBuddy host environment**: tell the user the library is unreachable in the current environment and it must run inside the WorkBuddy client with a logged-in account; do NOT search for other credentials, do NOT fall back to direct connection. No retry.
4. **`E_CONSENT_REQUIRED` — host-side authorization pending**: tell the user to complete authorization in the WorkBuddy client, then retry; do NOT retry on your own, do NOT bypass. Max 1 retry after the user confirms they have authorized.
5. **`E_ENDPOINT_UNTRUSTED` — host IPC endpoint cannot prove its identity**: stop immediately and say access was halted for safety; retry is forbidden, downgrading to any other channel is forbidden. No retry.
6. **`E_METHOD_UNKNOWN`, `E_METHOD_KIND_MISMATCH` — host capability missing**: tell the user to upgrade the WorkBuddy client, naming the missing channel capability; do NOT hard-try with tweaked params. No retry.
7. **`AUTH_REQUIRED` (host channel not connected or not opened) — not logged in or channel not authorized**: tell the user to log in and authorize in the WorkBuddy client, then retry; do NOT report as insufficient library permission, do NOT search other credentials. Max 1 retry.
8. **`12100`, `12607`, `56030`, `401` / `HTTP_401`, `403` / `HTTP_403` (except when the permission module says the capability is disabled) — insufficient permission**: report directly to the user, stating the current role (real role if known, else "not logged in or unknown role"), the missing permission, and the restricted `nodeId` / `spaceId`. No retry.
9. **`56161` — re-import permission (dedicated, not generic 403)**: this is a re-import (`import_html.py` carries `--node-block-id`) and the user has only editor role. Tell the user re-import requires admin; guide to AI editing — `page/edit-flow.md` via `page/entry.md` §Routing; editor role suffices for transactional incremental edit. Copy in `page/import-flow.md` §7.1. No re-import retry; switch to AI editing.
10. **`11510`, `404` / `HTTP_404`, `410` / `HTTP_410` — resource not found**: if the `nodeId` exists, re-resolve via `space.workspace.node-info` once; else re-resolve from a valid link (the old path is marked invalid). No repeat old path.
11. **`11112`, `19901`, `56039`, `409` / `HTTP_409`, `423` / `HTTP_423` — state / version conflict**: re-read the latest state (the module's latest-read method) and rebuild per `mutation.md`; previous team goal confirmations and old transactions are void. No reuse.
12. **`18406`, `56029`, `501` / `HTTP_501`, `CAPABILITY_DISABLED`; permission-module `403` / `HTTP_403` from the apply/invite switch — capability not enabled**: state explicitly which capability is disabled and offer the available alternative. No retry.
13. **`619610` / `11511` (content safety), `56031` (personal → enterprise drive), `56032` (enterprise → personal drive), `56033` (cross-enterprise), `56034` (space owner only), `56035`–`56037` (space-restricted ops), `56041` (security disposition) — protected resource**: state the protection rule directly, naming which bracket rule and which restricted object. No retry.
14. **`429` / `HTTP_429` — rate limit**: stop the current consecutive calls and suggest pausing. No immediate retry.
15. **`50000`, `56038`, `500` / `HTTP_500`, `502` / `HTTP_502`, `503` / `HTTP_503`, `504` / `HTTP_504`, `NETWORK_ERROR`, `TEMPORARY_ERROR`, `INVALID_RESPONSE`, `UNKNOWN` — transient failure**: the mutation may have already succeeded — query state first via the module's read-only status query; only re-submit if status shows it did not land. No blind re-submit.
16. **`524` / `HTTP_524` — volume-triggered timeout**: the batch may have partially landed — read back what landed via the module's read-only status query, then resume in smaller batches (library doc: `doc/server_pitfalls.md` §3). Never re-submit the same oversized payload; splitting the payload, not retrying, is the fix.

Backend codes not listed above, and no-code errors that are not clearly local param validation, are handled as transient failure. Safe `msg` may be quoted to describe the symptom, but never overrides the retry rules above. Query state first, then decide whether user intervention is needed.
